figures.alt: Photo of a forest hillside in rain with a muddy brown stream cutting a bank held together by tree roots.
figures.caption: Water moves soil downhill while roots hold some of it in place.

figures.alt: Illustration of two adults in everyday jackets looking at a rain garden of native plants in a strip next to a parking lot, in light rain.
figures.caption: A rain garden soaks up some runoff. It helps, but it does not stop all flooding.

figures.alt: Photo of a sloped plastic tray with a sand channel and grass along one bank while water is poured at the top and carries sand down the channel.
figures.caption: The stream tray: compare how much sediment moves with and without plants or stones.

figures.alt: A hillside in the rain. 1 Atmosphere: rain falls from a cloud. 2 Hydrosphere: water runs down the bare right slope and cuts a channel. 3 Geosphere: soil and rock are carried downhill, and a rock sits at the bottom. 4 Biosphere: grass on the left slope has roots that hold the soil in place. The four spheres touch and change each other in one place.
figures.caption: One rainy hill shows all four spheres at work: air, water, rock and soil, and living things.

figures.alt: A side view of Earth’s water. On the left is the ocean, salt water, about 97 percent of all water. On the right are land, a mountain with ice and glaciers on top, a layer of fresh groundwater under the ground, and a small lake and river. About 3 percent of Earth’s water is fresh. Most of that fresh water is frozen in ice or underground. Lakes and rivers hold only a tiny part.
figures.caption: Where Earth’s water is: mostly salty ocean. The fresh water is mostly ice or underground, and lakes and rivers hold very little.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Sediment moved in the stream tray. No plants 12 spoonfuls, Stones model 7 spoonfuls, Grass model 4 spoonfuls.
figures.caption: Stream-tray test, sediment moved: no plants 12 spoonfuls, stones model 7, grass model 4.

figures.alt: A grid of 100 squares. 97 are blue for salty ocean water, 2 are yellow for frozen fresh water, 1 is green for fresh water underground. Lakes and rivers are less than one square, shown as a tiny dot.
figures.caption: If all of Earth’s water were 100 squares: about 97 are salty ocean, 2 are frozen fresh water, about 1 is fresh water underground, and lakes and rivers are less than one square, a tiny dot. Almost no liquid fresh water is easy to reach.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Runoff after a storm. Parking lot 10 buckets, Rain garden 6 buckets.
figures.caption: Runoff after a storm: parking lot 10 buckets, rain garden 6 buckets. A rain garden reduces runoff but does not stop all of it.
